newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil port worker talks with steel firm stall.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port worker talks with steel firm stall.

text.p: Brazilian port workers and steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) failed to make any headway in their most recent talks about a labor dispute at Santos port, the company said.
"The presentation of a joint proposal by the three unions, agreed during talks mediated by the state labor secretary Walter Barelli, did not occur," Cosipa said in a statement.

A union commission met Cosipa officials Thursday to discuss the company's decision to use its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at Santos, which has already triggered two strikes there as well as two national stoppages.
The stevedores' and cargo controllers' unions separately presented partial proposals relating to the loading of steel products, the company said.
Cosipa handles coal and mineral products in bulk, exports steel products and handles containers for third parties, a port spokeswoman said.
"The loading registrars' union has not so far presented any proposal for loading and unloading operations in Cosipa's private maritime terminal," the firm said.
Earlier this week, stevedores proposed a 40 percent cut in the size of their work teams and a reduction in the amount of overtime hours workers were eligible for.
"A comparative analysis of costs indicates that the cost of the stevedores' proposal is more than 400 percent higher than Cosipa's costs using its own workers at its private terminal," Cosipa said.
The unions have said they will continue to negotiate until April 30 but warned they could start a fresh strike as of May 1 if no solution had been found by then.
